title: Define Corner Algebra and Perceptual Tone Interpolator for Token Stability in Compact Controls
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: We will introduce a deterministic corner-radius system (Corner Algebra) plus a perceptual tone interpolator for color ramps to reduce regressions when scaling the design system for high-density UI. The goal is to provide a small, composable token surface that: a) guarantees consistent tactile press depth across button variants, b) produces predictable layer stacking for table rows and card charts, and c) provides a stable interpolation mechanism for accessible color ramps across light/dark and compact modes.

Why now: Recent regressions from ad-hoc radius scalars and linear color blending have caused subtle accessibility and layout drift in dense tables and compact action bars. This ticket scopes a design-level specification (algorithms + token names), a migration plan for the component library, and an acceptance criteria matrix with visual and automated checks.

Deliverables: 
- Corner Algebra spec (formula, token mappings, fallbacks)
- Perceptual Tone Interpolator spec (LCh-based interpolation rules, contrast anchors)
- Token naming proposal and deprecation timeline (old -> new mapping)
- Component guidance for buttons, table rows, charts, and form controls
- Figma file with token previews and snapshot variants (compact/comfortable/legacy)
- Engineering PR checklist and rollout plan with feature flags and opt-in tokens

Out of scope: full type scale overhaul (separate ticket), animation/press micro-interactions beyond depth semantics, platform-specific CSS variables — we will provide recommended tokens and runtime knobs but not change platform CSS loaders in this pass.
acceptance_criteria: Corner Algebra documented with examples for small/medium/large components and verified in Figma
Perceptual Tone Interpolator produces consistent 4.5:1 minimum contrast for body text at compact sizes across light and dark themes
Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost) show stable perceived press depth across density toggles in visual tests
Table row separators and chart overlays maintain layering order without visual halo artifacts after migration
Migration guide and deprecation mapping published; engineering has a rollout plan with feature flag and canary target
Automated visual snapshots added to CI covering compact/comfortable/legacy token sets
notes: Corner Algebra idea: define base corner unit (CU) as 2px; express radii as algebraic expressions using proportional anchors: CU * (1 + sqrt(sizeIndex) * radiusFactor). This keeps small radii perceptually distinct while scaling smoothly for larger containers.

Perceptual Tone Interpolator: use LCh interpolation with fixed chroma clamps and dynamic lightness anchors tied to semantic roles (background, surface, border, accent). Avoid linear RGB or sRGB interpolation which caused hue shifts in previous pass.
Token mapping example: 'radius-sm' -> 'corner.cu-1.0', 'radius-md' -> 'corner.cu-1.6', 'radius-lg' -> 'corner.cu-2.4' with computed CSS var tokens for runtime adjustments.
Contrast anchors: define three anchors per semantic ramp (text-on-bg, text-on-surface, muted-on-surface) with target contrasts 7:1, 4.5:1, and 3:1 respectively for scalable interpolation checks.
Charts: introduce overlay-elevation tokens (e.g., elevation.chart-layer-1..3) to standardize micro-shadow usage and avoid ad-hoc drop shadows from product teams.
Deprecation: mark legacy tokens as deprecated for 3 months; provide compatibility shim token set (legacy->corner algebra) in console runtime to minimize product churn.
Rollout approach: 1) internal canary for frontend-shell and internal dashboards 2) opt-in beta flag for selected customers (Dedicated customers) 3) full migration behind 'tokens.v2' runtime switch.

References: Figma mock: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/Corner-Algebra-Prototypes, PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/842, Confluence design brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TS/Corner+Algebra+and+Tone+Interpolator
implementation_notes: Engineering should expose 'corner.cu' runtime var (default 2px). Components compute CSS border-radius as calc(var(--corner-cu) * <multiplier>) to keep runtime scaling simple.
Provide JS utility for perceptual interpolation (LCh library wrapper) with cache for common ratios; fallback to sRGB for older browsers with a visible warning in console during migration.
Add visual regression snapshots for key components: Buttons (all states), Table rows (collapsed/expanded), Chart overlays (legend/highlight), Modal and Toast surfaces.
Performance: token computation must be memoized; do not introduce reflows on key interaction paths. Precompute radii and elevational token maps at server-side build step where possible.
Accessibility QA: test combinations of compact density + small type scale + high contrast mode; update a11y checklist with contrast anchors and recommended token overrides for extreme cases.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Perceptual interpolation may produce unexpected hues in edge-case palettes. Mitigation: clamp chroma and add per-palette exception list documented in the spec.
Risk: Runtime token switch causes layout jank on older clients. Mitigation: provide CSS variable fallbacks and perform canary rollout with telemetry to detect regressions.
Risk: Product teams adopt new tokens inconsistently. Mitigation: include codemods and lint rules to detect legacy token usage and ship migration PR template for common components.
